answer: A stake-backed reputation trellis makes fake identities expensive: every agent must lock a refundable deposit, like a bond of timber credits, before it can trade, and the deposit is slashed when peers catch duplicate or dishonest behavior. Newcomers start with low trust and earn higher limits only through verified work, so an attacker must fund each fake separately. A public mirror of reputation records lets anyone audit an identity's history before dealing, so cheap copies cannot hide behind fresh names. Costs scale with the number of fakes; honest agents pay nothing extra.
